scientific_intent.scientific_task: Pad compact matrix rows in place using a statically partitioned cooperative CPU/GPU pipeline
scientific_intent.mathematical_operation: For compact row-major m×n input, write m×(n+pad) output preserving every input bit and inserting positive-zero padding columns.
scientific_intent.discretization: Two task-aligned Float64 shapes256×127(+1) and256×503(+9), tiles8192=256threads×32privatevalues; six Float32alpha CPUtaskfractions0/.1/.25/.5/.75/1,12paths.
scientific_intent.accuracy_requirements: ExactinputIEEEbits including signedzero/subnormal, fullpaddedmatrix,16host+16GPUmatrixguards/path and fullCPU/GPUdependencyflags+16flagguards. Independentinputscatteroracle and taskpartitionenumeration, bothnative/CUDAjlfullartifactcomparisons allfive.
scientific_intent.precision_sensitivity: Float64 storage/copy, +0 insertion, Float32partitionmultiply/truncation; zero/subnormal signs preserved through UInt64bitcontract, no floating-error tolerance.
scientific_intent.community_use_case: Storage padding and layout preparation are reusable matrix/pipeline components; no original physical simulation or scientificdataset attribution.
scientific_intent.description: Original IMPACT2016 source implements CPU/GPU hybrid in-place data sliding with a load-completion flag chain. Historical Julia computes correct out-of-place padding but omits the hybrid pipeline; preserved intact, with a separate faithful study completion.
scientific_intent.provenance: Native README cites Gómez-Luna etal2015 Inplace data sliding algorithms for many-core architectures. The study retains original CPU/GPU algorithms but declares legal aligned finite fixtures and static partition scope.
